_comment: Early ends and returns (Expansion 6 E.4, game/story/early.py): a contingency's set piece, an endure step's beat (the letter it left to be delivered on its death, for a villain that speaks; the thing it kept caged and let loose, for one that does not), the word that a villain you put down walks again (it takes the tale on), and the villain moving its anchor into its own hall.

text: A rider you do not know comes up the road at a walk, holds out a sealed letter at arm's length, and turns back the way he came without a word. The seal is {villain_short}'s.
A boy brings it, paid in advance by somebody who is dead now: a letter, sealed with {villain_short}'s seal, to be put in your hand on the day {he} died.
It is left where you will find it, pinned under a stone on the road ahead: a letter in {villain_short}'s hand, written before {he} died, and meant for you.
When you look up from it, there are figures on the rise, spreading out. They have been waiting for the letter to reach you.
You are still reading when you hear them: {villain_short}'s people, come to carry out the last of {his} orders.
There is a whistle from the trees. The letter was to keep you standing still.

label: Read it, and face them.
result: You put the letter away and draw.
There will be time to think about what it said, after.

label: Drop it and run for it.
result: You are away before they close, and you do not stop until dark. They do not follow.
You run, and keep running, and when you finally stop there is nobody behind you.
fail_result: They are faster than you, and they know the ground. You turn to face them.
You do not get far. There is no way out but through them.

text: {villain_short} is dead, and what it kept is not kept any more. You hear them before you see them: things that were held for this, let loose to find you.
Whatever {villain_short} kept close to it is loose now that it is gone, and hungry, and it has your scent.
There is a sound in the dark that you have heard before, near {home}. What {villain_short} gathered around it did not die with it.

label: Stand and meet them.
result: If they want you, they will have to come and take you.

label: Break the trail and lose them.
result: Through water and over stone, and back on yourselves twice. By dawn there is nothing on your trail.
You know the old tricks, and they are enough. They lose you at the river.
fail_result: They will not be shaken off. They are on you before you have gone a mile.
Every trick you know, and it is not enough. They come out of the dark all at once.

title: {villain}
text: The news finds you on the road, and it is the news you were afraid of: {villain} walks again. They say it was seen at {home}, and that it asked for you by name.
You hear it twice in one day, from people who do not know each other: {villain} is back. What you put down did not stay down.
A carter from {town} tells you, as if you would not believe it: {villain} has come back. The old women were right to keep the iron on their doors.

label: Then I will finish it. (A tale begins: the journal keeps it.)
result: You have done it once. You can do it again, and this time do it properly.
This time you will find what binds it, before you go in.

label: Not now.
result: It will still be there. That is the trouble with it.
Someone else, perhaps. Or you, later.

text: Word comes from those who watch for you: something was carried out of its hiding place by night, under guard, and taken to {home}.
A shepherd saw them pass in the dark, a long line of them, carrying something between them with great care, towards {home}.
You dream of a dark hall, and of hands laying something down in it, and you wake knowing that {villain_short} has moved what binds {him}.
